summary: Standing playbook (full text: executiveagent/docs/GRANT_APPLICATION_PLAYBOOK.md) — the grant-cycle process Michelle Rogers runs for Interplanetary Fund, learned from the supervised worked example of 2026-11-28. PROCESS: (1) Research open opportunities, recording amount, deadline, eligibility, fee, and source for each candidate. (2) Rank by fit — non-dilutive and free-to-apply first; pre-revenue explicitly welcome outranks larger prizes that quietly expect traction; no recurring costs ever; women-founder eligibility (>=50% women-owned) matches the company as constituted; deadline realism counts. (3) Verify deadlines, amounts, fees, and eligibility on the funder's own page before treating them as fact; anything unverified is labelled UNVERIFIED. Flag every fee and note whether a waiver exists. (4) Prepare the shared application core once per cycle: business description (AI-powered fundraising/crowdfunding platform, live product, pre-revenue, bootstrapped, solo woman founder in Everett, WA), founder bio skeleton from confirmed facts only, and a use-of-funds narrative that is truthful and specific — no invented revenue, user counts, projections, testimonials, or urgency, and no private founder circumstances in copy unless a form explicitly asks and the owner approves. (5) Per application: map every field before filling; a field with no truthful source stays blank and goes on the gap list; NEVER invent entity type, EIN, founding date, revenue, ownership details, bank details, or dates of birth. (6) STOP for owner approval before any fee payment, before any final submission, before signing or uploading identity/financial documents, and before representing entity form, revenue, or ownership beyond what is confirmed. (7) Record every application same-day in public.executive_opportunities with status and next_action always set (amount_verified only for funder-stated amounts); follow-ups also become executive.tasks with due_at. (8) File what was learned after each cycle under department funding. Deadlines are kept in the funder's timezone (the November 2026 cluster closed 11:59pm ET = 8:59pm in Everett). WORKED EXAMPLE (researched 2026-11-28; re-verify before any future round): four grants closing Mon 30 Nov 2026, 11:59pm ET — Amber Grant (WomensNet; 3 x $15,000 this month plus a 3 x $75,000 year-end pool for monthly winners; November is the STEM category month; one form also enters the Startup Grant, for which pre-revenue with <$10k sales qualifies; $15 fee, waiver on request by email; recurs monthly, each re-entry a new fee decision); Hey Helen Grant (Visionaries; $10,000/month unrestricted; $15 fee; ONE application stays on file for 12 monthly rounds — best fee efficiency; requires a US business bank account; pre-revenue eligible); IFundWomen Startup Accelerator Grant ($5,000 unrestricted, no equity; $5 fee, waiver in advance per rules; idea-stage and pre-revenue explicitly welcome; winner expected ~15 Dec 2026; funder is IFundWomen — no affiliation with Interplanetary Fund); HerRise MicroGrant (HerSuiteSpot; $1,000/month, 1 winner; $15 non-refundable fee; filed in the example only because the narrative was already drafted; recurs monthly, closing the last day of the month). Total November-cluster fees if all paid: $50 before waivers. Followed by Verizon Small Business Digital Ready Grant ($10,000, FREE; unlock the application by completing any 2 free Digital Ready courses/events by 7 Dec 2026; decisions by 12 Jan 2027; taxable via LISC 1099; lesson: the course-unlock step, not the form, is the schedule risk — start courses the week the grant is identified). CADENCE: Amber and HerRise recur monthly (re-entry = new fee approval each time); Hey Helen stays on file (verify the entry is live rather than re-applying); IFundWomen Universal Grant Application is free and done once alongside any IFundWomen round; Galaxy Grant ($3,500, free, closes 31 Jan 2027) and Women Founders Grant ($5,000, closes 31 Dec 2026, $25 fee, for-profit funder — a conscious owner decision) are longer-fuse items; NSF SBIR/STTR (up to ~$305,000 Phase I) is genuine-R&D funding and a deliberate Q1-2027 project, never a monthly-cycle rush. Honest negative from the example: no currently open general Washington-state or Snohomish County grant for a pre-revenue tech startup was verified — do not manufacture local options. OWNER-SUPPLIED FACTS (names only; values are never stored in knowledge, notes, or the playbook): legal business name, legal entity type, EIN, founding/formation date, state of registration, business address, ownership percentages, business bank account status, revenue/sales to date, employee/contractor count, founder date of birth where a funder requires it, business phone/email, prior grants/loans/outside capital, student enrolment status and level.
title: Grant application playbook — process, discipline, and the November 2026 worked example (Amber, Hey Helen, IFundWomen, HerRise, Verizon Digital Ready)
